Conversations are far more interesting when people interact during the conversation. It is important to ask for others' opinions on a subject as well as giving your own.

Here are some ways you can ask for and give opinions.

I believe people are worried about the working conditions.

Adjectives are words used before nouns. They give information about the nouns and indicate qualities. They can also be used to describe your feelings and or things like the weather.

1. “-ing” adjectives are used to describe opinions, feelings, and things.
    Examples:
    • The whole experience was terrifying.
    • The storm was a frightening experience.

  2. “-ed” adjectives are used to describe how people feel.
    Examples:
    • I was terrified when the power went out.
    • I was frightened by all the loud noises.
Here's a table to help you understand “-ed” and “-ing” adjectives.

images.text:
Janet: Hi, Peter. Would you mind coming in?
Peter: No problem. How are you? Did you read through my proposal by any chance?
Janet: Good, thanks. Yes and to be honest, I was pleased with it. It only needed minor adjustments.
Peter: I'm happy that my work was satisfying. Could you possibly do me a favor?
Janet: Just a minute Peter. Could I ask you to notify us the next time you are unable to come into work? We were worried about you.

Peter: No problem. The storm last night was terrifying. There were fallen trees everywhere in my neighborhood. I was lucky not to have been crushed by one. I believe you must have been worried about your employees. I thought it would be understood why I wasn't in the next day.
Janet: Did you have a close call?
Peter: I think the whole weather situation was disturbing and frightening.
Janet: Personally, I'm glad to hear you're okay. You had us worried.

Peter: How did you manage to get home under the conditions?
Janet: It was reassuring to know that the storm wasn't too damaging.
Peter: That's amazing ... Janet, I feel exhausted after this experience. I would like to request a week off. To my mind, I'm sure I will be more productive.
Janet: Of course, you deserve it. I know you've been wanting some time off. I reckon things are calmer now. Could you please call the office if anything unexpected comes up?
Peter: Sure. Thank you Janet.
